explanation: Reference checked (SQL re-run + independent Python computation on the CSV files: 487980). Qwen never uses the reference date 2026-09-26: it compares the birth date with the order date (o.date). Its birthday window is also contradictory: mm-dd(order) >= mm-dd(birth) AND mm-dd(order) < mm-dd(birth + 26 years), and birth + 26 years has the same month-day as the birth date, so the condition is always false. No line matches and the value is 0; the 6 customers aged exactly 25 on 2026-09-26 (C001, C002, C003, C007, C008, C009) are all missed.

Reference checked (SQL re-run + independent Python computation: 558980). Completed age at the order date is computed with an off-by-one: branch 1 (year difference = 25 and birthday already reached) is correct, but branch 2 (year difference = 24 and birthday not yet reached) selects customers aged 23 instead of 25. The valid case 'year difference = 26 and birthday not yet reached' is missing, so the orders of customers born in 2000 placed before their 2026 birthday are lost (C004, C005, C007, C022: 439570 cents). Value too low.

Reference checked (SQL re-run + independent Python computation: 168680). The period filter is correct, but the age filter ignores the birth year and only compares month-day strings, with two contradictory conditions: mm-dd(birth) <= '09-25' AND mm-dd(birth) > '09-25'. This is always false, so no line matches and the value is 0; the 5 customers aged 25 on 2026-09-25 with orders in the period (C001, C002, C005, C007, C008) are missed.

Reference checked (SQL re-run + independent Python computation: 258180). Products and period are correct. The age is hard-coded by birth year with the birthday boundary inverted: born 2001 with mm-dd < '09-25', or born 2000 with mm-dd >= '09-25'. It excludes C001 (born 2001-09-25, exactly 25 on 2026-09-25, -80190 cents) and includes C004 (born 2000-09-25, already 26 that day, +70500 cents). Net gap 9690 cents. Under the protocol, completed age changes on the birthday itself.

Reference checked (SQL re-run + independent Python computation: 1990). Product d and the period are correct, but the age test compares a year string with a full date: strftime('%Y', date(birth_date,'+25 years')) <= '2026-09-25'. As text, '2026' <= '2026-09-25' is true (prefix), so the test only means 'born in 2001 or earlier' (2002 or earlier in the second branch), not 'exactly 25'. Nine extra customers are counted, e.g. C013 born 1958, C058 born 1990 and C014 born 2001-12-08 (24 on the reference date): value too high.
